industry.why: Overweight, carried, and I am declining the row's own written condition for Double Overweight, said plainly: 'to A if relative strength reaches B with defensives still leading at three months' is met on its letter. Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: B now, D prior (C at last week's reading), and the three-month defensives-against-cyclicals line is +6.3 points. Not taken because the condition was written to confirm a strengthening rotation and this week the rotation weakened on every window (one week -1.0 from +2.6, four weeks +3.0 from +5.6, six months +1.4 from +3.7, twelve months -0.6 from +1.9), breadth broadened for a third week with the index at its high, and the rate read that makes staples the destination is three weeks stale with the headlines running against it. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). Relative strength reaching B describes a move already made; raising a defensive to the top letter in the week its lead narrows would buy the crowded end of it. Three live holdings (Carlsberg 4.62%, Fevertree 2.49%, Hilton Food 4.75%, 11.86 points) sit here. Counter-case: this is the goalpost-moving I refused on Consumer discretionary last week, and Richard may prefer the rule to the judgement. To A if the industry holds B at the next reading with defensives leading again at one week, four weeks and three months; to C if the three-month line falls under +2 points.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': non-discretionary demand and proven cases, with the pay floor rising 3.9% in April 2027 against 4.1% in April 2026 and food tariffs cut. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): staples are the destination of the rotation to defensives, and Nestlé's 4.3% pet care growth read across to ingredients (Jefferies, 23 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: C now, D prior, the market has started to pay. One live holding, Hilton Food (3.30%, Fitness 77.8). Counter-case: input-cost inflation squeezes producers before it reaches retailers. Moves to A with the staples industry if defensives lead for a second month.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the Bank of England's decision of 5-Nov-26 is still unread and the headlines disagree on it (on hold according to MarketScreener, cutting in 2026 according to the Irish Examiner, both undated); a weaker November consumer confidence headline (Trading Economics, undated) was not confirmed as a print for the window. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book is 39% UK-listed by invested weight (component 5). Balanced on unread evidence, so Neutral is an absence here, not a judgement. To D on hawkish guidance when the decision is read; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
